// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// OpenZeppelin Contracts (last updated v4.9.0) (token/ERC20/extensions/IERC20Permit.sol)

pragma solidity ^0.8.0;

/**
 * @dev Interface of the ERC20 Permit extension allowing approvals to be made via signatures, as defined in
 * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612[EIP-2612].
 *
 * Adds the {permit} method, which can be used to change an account's ERC20 allowance (see {IERC20-allowance}) by
 * presenting a message signed by the account. By not relying on {IERC20-approve}, the token holder account doesn't
 * need to send a transaction, and thus is not required to hold Ether at all.
 */
interface IERC20Permit {
    /**
     * @dev Sets `value` as the allowance of `spender` over ``owner``'s tokens,
     * given ``owner``'s signed approval.
     *
     * IMPORTANT: The same issues {IERC20-approve} has related to transaction
     * ordering also apply here.
     *
     * Emits an {Approval} event.
     *
     * Requirements:
     *
     * - `spender` cannot be the zero address.
     * - `deadline` must be a timestamp in the future.
     * - `v`, `r` and `s` must be a valid `secp256k1` signature from `owner`
     * over the EIP712-formatted function arguments.
     * - the signature must use ``owner``'s current nonce (see {nonces}).
     *
     * For more information on the signature format, see the
     * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612#specification[relevant EIP
     * section].
     */
    function permit(
        address owner,
        address spender,
        uint256 value,
        uint256 deadline,
        uint8 v,
        bytes32 r,
        bytes32 s
    ) external;

    /**
     * @dev Returns the current nonce for `owner`. This value must be
     * included whenever a signature is generated for {permit}.
     *
     * Every successful call to {permit} increases ``owner``'s nonce by one. This
     * prevents a signature from being used multiple times.
     */
    function nonces(address owner) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @dev Returns the domain separator used in the encoding of the signature for {permit}, as defined by {EIP712}.
     */
    // solhint-disable-next-line func-name-mixedcase
    function DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() external view returns (bytes32);
}

selectedFunctions.label: Umami Cancel own pending GM BTC vault request
warnings: Static exact-deployment ABI/source inventory only; no runtime identity, execution, liquidity, funding, complete-workflow or financial-safety assurance. Independent grants, pause checks and canonical-calldata controls remain mandatory.

Only Arbitrum gmUSDC BTC-backed vault 0x5f851F67D24419982EcD7b7765deFD64fBb50a97 is selected, not old GLP vaults or the ETH-backed gmUSDC whose deposit pause was observed. Underlying is 6-decimal native USDC 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, not bridged USDC.e; vault shares also have 6 decimals.

Deposit transfers caller USDC into this vault using allowance to this vault, then forwards a request to its configured aggregate vault. Receiver is explicit; zero is rejected in the bundled aggregate source. The immediate return value is an estimate, not minted-share or settlement confirmation. No standalone prefunding is admitted.

Redeem escrows owner shares in this vault rather than immediately burning/paying them. Owner must approve the vault to transfer shares even when owner equals caller; a different caller additionally consumes owner-to-caller share allowance. Receiver controls settlement destination, whereas cancellation refunds the recorded initiating sender, not necessarily owner or receiver.

Both deposit and redeem are payable because msg.value is forwarded to the aggregate for keeper execution gas, not ETH principal. Bundled aggregate code requires msg.value >= configured gas requirement times tx.gasprice and forwards all supplied value to rebalanceKeeper, without an excess refund in these entrypoints; documented approximately 0.001 ETH is not a fixed fee quote.

minOutAfterFees is forwarded into the pending request without local enforcement. Bundled aggregate source stores it for deferred execution; current exact aggregate/request-handler source and minimum-enforcement implementation were not independently bound, and no live execution/min-output guarantee is asserted. No caller deadline is present.

Conversions floor at the share price and dynamic fees can consume small inputs; deposit requires nonzero preview shares and capacity, redeem requires nonzero preview assets and sufficient aggregate USDC before it can even queue. Documented fees are 2% annual management and 20% yield plus dynamic entry/exit fees; actual configured execution-time rates may differ.

Requests depend on keeper/oracle execution, configured hooks, buffers and rebalancing; no fixed settlement delay or payout guarantee. cancelRequest checks exact vault and initiating sender, returns escrowed USDC or shares and clears the pending request; already cleared/executed or unavailable escrow requests can revert, and keeper ETH is not refunded by this function.

Explorer snapshot reports depositPaused=false, withdrawalPaused=false, aggregateVault=0x1E914730B4Cd343aE14530F0BBF6b350d83B833d and asset=USDC. These are point-in-time reported values, not persistence or runtime attestation. Configurator can pause operations or replace aggregateVault; the immutable AUTH reference is not automatically replaced with it.

Caller-selected callback variants, permit, approvals/transfers, privileged share accounting, pause/configuration and all views are excluded. The fixed configured aggregate dependency may revert or change; its source bundled in the vault compilation is contextual only, not an independently verified current deployed aggregate ABI. Umami requires lawful jurisdictional participation; no KYC eligibility or legal suitability is inferred.

sourceSemantics.deposit(uint256,uint256,address): AssetVault.deposit: require positive preview shares and cap; caller USDC safeTransferFrom to vault; aggregate.handleDeposit with caller, explicit receiver, zero callback and all msg.value. Returned shares is pre-execution preview; actual accounting is deferred.
sourceSemantics.redeem(uint256,uint256,address,address): AssetVault.redeem: positive shares, integer share-to-asset conversion, owner-to-caller allowance if distinct, aggregate cash check, nonzero preview; safeTransferFrom(owner,vault,shares) requires owner-to-vault allowance; forwards caller, receiver, zero callback and all msg.value to aggregate.handleWithdraw. No local settlement.
sourceSemantics.cancelRequest(uint256): Read aggregate.getRequest(key); require request.vault=this and request.sender=msg.sender; refund request.amount of underlying for deposit or this share token for redemption to sender, then aggregate.clearRequest(key). No arbitrary request modification or target parameter.
sourceSemantics.minimaAndFees: minOutAfterFees forwarded unchanged; bundled aggregate stores pending-request constraint and pays all native fee to keeper. Exact current handler enforcement is not claimed. ShareMath floors integer division. Dynamic fee previews call configured aggregate.
sourceSemantics.authority: GlobalACL uses immutable constructor AUTH. Configurator can update aggregateVault independently. PausableVault has distinct mutable deposit/withdraw flags initialized false; live explorer snapshot distinguishes current state from constructor state.

# Vault Tokens & Contract Addresses

Repository of Contract for Umami's GM Vaults

Deposits in Umami's GM Vaults are represented by tokens implemented using the ERC-4626 standard for each respective vault. If the respective Vault generates a profit, PPS (Price Per Share) of your token will increase in relation to the underlying token of your Vault. Each individual Vault is represented by specific tokens.

# Asset Buffer & Withdraws

Understand GM Vaults Withdrawal Process

**Asset Buffer** \
Umami's GM Vaults are designed to limit the impact of price changes in the non-deposit assets that are part of GMI. The vaults manage Delta by automatically reducing extra exposure through hedging. Regular rebalancing to effectively hedge plays a critical role in this process. Given that rebalancing can be complex and relatively costly, the strategy employs an Asset Buffer to bypass constant rebalancing. \
\
This entails reserving a small portion of the deposited assets, not using them to mint GM tokens but instead setting them aside. 

Asset Buffer of ETH backed market: [0x0Ca62954b46AfEe430D645dA493C6C783448C4eD](https://arbiscan.io/address/0x0ca62954b46afee430d645da493c6c783448c4ed)

Asset Buffer of BTC backed market: [0x1E914730B4Cd343aE14530F0BBF6b350d83B833d](https://arbiscan.io/address/0x1e914730b4cd343ae14530f0bbf6b350d83b833d)\
\
**Withdraws** \
Please note that currently, the vaults do not automatically rebalance when this buffer is used up. So, if you want to withdraw a large amount of assets (more than the buffer amount), you'll have to wait for a rebalance to refill the buffer. We will be implementing a withdrawal queue where users can request their withdraw to be available on the next rebalance to better optimize this experience. \
\
Note: GMX has circuit breakers on their GM markets that prevent withdraws while open interest has exceeded TVL, The Vaults source their yield from the GMI which is an index of GM markets and currently the index works as a single unit, meaning if one pool has tripped a circuit breaker the full Vault is unable to rebalance. This will soon be a non-issue with an upcoming upgrade to the Vaults. \
\
**Alternative Liquidity Options** \
Your deposit will be represented by an ERC-4626 token, enabling composability with various external DeFi protocols. This gives you alternative ways to access liquidity without needing to use the standard withdrawal function on Umami's user interface. For example, you can participate in Uniswap LPs if the community creates one or soon leverage your position through borrowing or looping on money market protocols.

Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://about.umami.finance/umami-finance/gm-vaults/gm-fee-structure.md). # GM Fee Structure ### **Fee Table**
Fee TypeValue
Vault Usage fee (per annum)2%
Approx. Yield Fee (annual equiv)20%
### **Deposit and Withdrawal Fees** Deposit and withdrawal fees are calculated dynamically at the time of transaction execution. These fees are based on the weight of the asset being deposited or withdrawn in the index and the weight of the GM tokens in the index, plus an additional 0.1%. The total fees for both deposits and withdrawals are expected to be **around 0.1% to 0.2%.** The additional 0.1% is allocated to cover position management fees associated with external positions undertaken by the vault. All the fees collected from deposits and withdrawals are fully utilized for the operation of the vault and are not transferred to the treasury. ### Execution Fee A ETH execution fee is required at the time of deposit and withdrawal to cover the keeper gas cost for the position execution and chainlink low latency feed fee. This is approximately to 0.001 ETH.

limitations: Static exact-deployment ABI/source inventory only; no runtime identity, execution, liquidity, funding, complete-workflow or financial-safety assurance. Independent grants, pause checks and canonical-calldata controls remain mandatory.

Only Arbitrum gmUSDC BTC-backed vault 0x5f851F67D24419982EcD7b7765deFD64fBb50a97 is selected, not old GLP vaults or the ETH-backed gmUSDC whose deposit pause was observed. Underlying is 6-decimal native USDC 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, not bridged USDC.e; vault shares also have 6 decimals.

Deposit transfers caller USDC into this vault using allowance to this vault, then forwards a request to its configured aggregate vault. Receiver is explicit; zero is rejected in the bundled aggregate source. The immediate return value is an estimate, not minted-share or settlement confirmation. No standalone prefunding is admitted.

Redeem escrows owner shares in this vault rather than immediately burning/paying them. Owner must approve the vault to transfer shares even when owner equals caller; a different caller additionally consumes owner-to-caller share allowance. Receiver controls settlement destination, whereas cancellation refunds the recorded initiating sender, not necessarily owner or receiver.

Both deposit and redeem are payable because msg.value is forwarded to the aggregate for keeper execution gas, not ETH principal. Bundled aggregate code requires msg.value >= configured gas requirement times tx.gasprice and forwards all supplied value to rebalanceKeeper, without an excess refund in these entrypoints; documented approximately 0.001 ETH is not a fixed fee quote.

minOutAfterFees is forwarded into the pending request without local enforcement. Bundled aggregate source stores it for deferred execution; current exact aggregate/request-handler source and minimum-enforcement implementation were not independently bound, and no live execution/min-output guarantee is asserted. No caller deadline is present.

Conversions floor at the share price and dynamic fees can consume small inputs; deposit requires nonzero preview shares and capacity, redeem requires nonzero preview assets and sufficient aggregate USDC before it can even queue. Documented fees are 2% annual management and 20% yield plus dynamic entry/exit fees; actual configured execution-time rates may differ.

Requests depend on keeper/oracle execution, configured hooks, buffers and rebalancing; no fixed settlement delay or payout guarantee. cancelRequest checks exact vault and initiating sender, returns escrowed USDC or shares and clears the pending request; already cleared/executed or unavailable escrow requests can revert, and keeper ETH is not refunded by this function.

Explorer snapshot reports depositPaused=false, withdrawalPaused=false, aggregateVault=0x1E914730B4Cd343aE14530F0BBF6b350d83B833d and asset=USDC. These are point-in-time reported values, not persistence or runtime attestation. Configurator can pause operations or replace aggregateVault; the immutable AUTH reference is not automatically replaced with it.

Caller-selected callback variants, permit, approvals/transfers, privileged share accounting, pause/configuration and all views are excluded. The fixed configured aggregate dependency may revert or change; its source bundled in the vault compilation is contextual only, not an independently verified current deployed aggregate ABI. Umami requires lawful jurisdictional participation; no KYC eligibility or legal suitability is inferred.
